justice: Complete lack of sidewalks and curb ramps structurally excludes wheelchair users and the elderly from accessing the space
The wide asphalt lanes are exclusively allocated to motor vehicles, reflecting extremely poor spatial equity for active, non-motorized users
The absence of tactile paving and pedestrian pathways completely ignores the navigational needs of visually impaired individuals
safety: Continuous metal guardrails along the edges effectively prevent motor vehicles from veering off the elevated roadway
Clear white lane markings and overhead green directional signs support safe and predictable navigation for drivers
The complete lack of pedestrian and cyclist infrastructure exposes any potential vulnerable road users to fatal risks from high-speed traffic
livability: The environment completely lacks commercial facades, residential buildings, or community facilities to support daily human activities
There are zero public benches, resting spots, or plazas to facilitate social interaction for teenagers or the elderly
The dominance of the highway ramp infrastructure creates an exclusionary zone with absolute zero street-level vitality
sustainability: The presence of the large white coach bus in the center lane indicates usage of the corridor for collective public transit
The expansive impermeable asphalt road surface lacks any visible stormwater drainage or bioswale integration
While roadside trees and shrubs are visible, they act merely as distant visual buffers rather than integrated, accessible urban green infrastructure
aesthetics: Massive high-voltage transmission towers and overhead power lines dominate the skyline, creating a harsh industrial aesthetic
The unbroken expanse of grey asphalt and continuous metal guardrails lacks visual diversity and human-scale design elements
Peripheral green vegetation offers the only natural visual relief against the heavily engineered, utilitarian highway structure
comfort: The unshaded expanse of the multi-lane road offers no thermal comfort or canopy protection against direct sun exposure
The complete absence of benches or shelters provides zero physical comfort or resting opportunities for vulnerable pedestrians
High-speed vehicular traffic on the open asphalt induces severe psychological discomfort and noise stress for anyone outside a vehicle
walkability: The total absence of paved sidewalks makes walking fundamentally impossible and highly dangerous for pedestrians
There are no marked crosswalks, pedestrian signals, or safe crossing points across the wide vehicular lanes
The elevated ramp design and continuous guardrail barriers physically block any pedestrian route connectivity or access
bikeability: No dedicated or painted bike lanes exist on the asphalt surface, providing zero safe spaces for cyclists
The highway interchange geometry and high-speed vehicular merging zones create an inherently lethal environment for cycling
